title: Triangular integral divided-adjoint coefficient at the bottom of a root string
statement:
Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional split semisimple Lie algebra over $\mathbf Q$ [def-wf-lie-algebra, def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], with splitting Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, reduced crystallographic root system $R$, positive roots $R^+$, and simple roots $\Delta$. Fix a Chevalley basis in the conventions of [lem-sfb-kostant-integral-pbw]: the simple coroots $h_i$ form a basis of $\mathfrak h$, the nonzero $e_\gamma$ span the root spaces, $[h,e_\gamma]=\gamma(h)e_\gamma$, $[e_\gamma,e_{-\gamma}]=h_\gamma$, and $[e_\gamma,e_\delta]=\pm(p_{\gamma,\delta}+1)e_{\gamma+\delta}$ for a root sum, where $p_{\gamma,\delta}=\max\{q\geq0:\delta-q\gamma\in R\}$; the bracket is zero if the sum is neither a root nor zero. Put $U=T_{\mathbf Q}(\mathfrak g)/(xy-yx-[x,y])$ and $e_\gamma^{(m)}=e_\gamma^m/m!$. Let $a,b\in R^+$ be linearly independent with $b-a\notin R$, and let $k\geq1$ satisfy $\gamma=b+ka\in R$. Fix any total order on $R^+$. There is a sign $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$ with $(\operatorname{ad}e_a)^k(e_b)/k!=\varepsilon e_\gamma$ such that, for every $n\geq1$, the element
$$\sum_{j=0}^{kn}(-1)^j e_a^{(kn-j)}e_b^{(n)}e_a^{(j)}-\varepsilon^n e_\gamma^{(n)}$$
is a finite integer linear combination of ordered monomials $\prod_{\delta\in R^+}e_\delta^{(r_\delta)}$ with $0\leq r_\delta<n$ for every $\delta$. Each monomial with nonzero coefficient can be required to have total root weight $\sum_\delta r_\delta\delta=n\gamma$, and every root occurring in it lies in $R\cap\{u a+v b:u\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0},\ v\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}\}$. An empty linear combination is allowed.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, printed pp.508--509, for the assumed normalization; agent-stated local coefficient lemma supporting the simple divided-power generation asserted via Mathieu Section 1, pp.150--151. Proposed proof uses the existing integral and rational PBW nodes, not a theorem explicitly stated by Milne. Full source WANTED: Kostant, Groups over Z (1966), integral-form construction; Steinberg, Lectures on Chevalley Groups (1967), integral-form construction.

proof.text: Index the root/coroot pairing by $R$, with root map $\delta\mapsto\delta\in\mathfrak h^\vee$, coroot map $\delta\mapsto h_\delta\in\mathfrak h$, and evaluation pairing. These are precisely the finite crystallographic root-pairing data of the assumed root system (the ambient duality is perfect). Apply [lem-sfb-root-string-integer-interval] to the independent roots $a,b$. Since $b-a$ is absent, its interval has bottom endpoint zero; write its top endpoint as $q$. Thus $b+ia$ is a root exactly for integers $0\le i\le q$, and $k\le q$. For $0\le i<q$, the largest $p$ with $(b+ia)-pa$ a root is $i$. The assumed Chevalley bracket formula therefore gives $[e_a,e_{b+ia}]=\eta_i(i+1)e_{b+(i+1)a}$ with $\eta_i\in\{1,-1\}$. Put $X=e_a$ and $D(u)=Xu-uX$. Induction gives $Y_i=D^i(e_b)/i!=c_i e_{b+ia}$, where $c_0=1$ and $c_{i+1}=\eta_i c_i$, for $0\le i\le q$; all subsequent $Y_i$ vanish because $b+(q+1)a$ is neither a root nor zero. Take $\varepsilon=c_k$.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, printed pp.508--509; agent reconstruction of the supporting divided-adjoint coefficient argument using the cited PBW statements (not a theorem stated in Milne).

proof.text: In formal series with central variable $t$, put $E(t)=\sum_{r\ge0}X^rt^r/r!$. Coefficientwise the binomial identity gives $E(-t)E(t)=1$. For any $u\in U$, induction on $m$ in $D(u)=Xu-uX$ gives $D^m(u)=\sum_{j=0}^m(-1)^j\binom mj X^{m-j}uX^j$: the induction step combines the two adjacent terms by Pascal's identity. Consequently $E(t)uE(-t)=\sum_{m\ge0}D^m(u)t^m/m!$. In particular $E(t)e_bE(-t)=Y(t)=\sum_{i=0}^qY_it^i$. Cancelling $E(-t)E(t)$ between consecutive factors proves $E(t)e_b^{(n)}E(-t)=Y(t)^n/n!$. All identities are coefficientwise finite, so no analytic exponential or convergence is involved.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, printed pp.508--509; agent reconstruction of the supporting divided-adjoint coefficient argument using the cited PBW statements (not a theorem stated in Milne).

proof.text: Write $A_n=[t^{kn}]Y(t)^n/n!$. The previous identity identifies $A_n$ with $\sum_{j=0}^{kn}(-1)^j e_a^{(kn-j)}e_b^{(n)}e_a^{(j)}$. Expanding the finite polynomial $Y(t)^n$ expresses $A_n$ as a rational sum of words of length $n$ in $e_{b+ia}$, with indices $i_1+\cdots+i_n=kn$. Each word has weight $n b+kn a=n\gamma$. Let $S=R\cap\{ua+vb:u\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0},\ v\in\mathbf Z_{\ge1}\}$. Then $S\subset R^+$, each word uses only $S$, and $S$ is closed under root sums that are roots. Two roots in $S$ cannot be opposite or sum to zero, since their $b$-coordinates are positive and $a,b$ are independent.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, printed pp.508--509; agent reconstruction of the supporting divided-adjoint coefficient argument using the cited PBW statements (not a theorem stated in Milne).

proof.text: Sort each word of Step 3 into the prescribed positive-root order using $e_\rho e_\sigma=e_\sigma e_\rho+[e_\rho,e_\sigma]$. The bracket is zero or a scalar times $e_{\rho+\sigma}$ by the assumed normalization. Termination and the required properties follow by induction on word length, then on inversions at fixed length: a swap reduces inversions, while each bracket correction has one fewer factor. Corrections stay in $S$ and preserve weight. The resulting rational expansion of $A_n$ uses ordered positive monomials of length at most $n$, supported in $S$, all of weight $n\gamma$. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-pbw] to the full ordered Chevalley basis (negative roots, Cartan basis, positive roots in the specified order). It makes this ordered expansion unique, and its filtration clause identifies length with PBW degree. Changing ordinary powers to divided powers multiplies coefficients by factorials and changes none of these supports or degrees.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, printed pp.508--509; agent reconstruction of the supporting divided-adjoint coefficient argument using the cited PBW statements (not a theorem stated in Milne).

proof.text: In length exactly $n$, sorting has only permuted the $n$ original factors; every bracket correction has smaller length. Thus the coefficient of the ordinary monomial $e_\gamma^n$ comes only from the tuple $i_1=\cdots=i_n=k$ in $Y(t)^n/n!$. Its coefficient is $c_k^n/n!=\varepsilon^n/n!$, so the coefficient of $e_\gamma^{(n)}$ is $\varepsilon^n$. Moreover if any ordered monomial in Step 4 has an exponent $r_\delta\ge n$, its length bound forces $r_\delta=n$ and every other exponent zero. Its weight equation gives $n\delta=n\gamma$, hence $\delta=\gamma$ over $\mathbf Q$. Subtracting $\varepsilon^n e_\gamma^{(n)}$ therefore removes every possible exponent at least $n$.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, printed pp.508--509; agent reconstruction of the supporting divided-adjoint coefficient argument using the cited PBW statements (not a theorem stated in Milne).

proof.text: Each summand in the displayed formula for $A_n$ is a product of root divided powers, hence belongs to the unital integer subalgebra $U_{\mathbf Z}$ in [lem-sfb-kostant-integral-pbw]. That node supplies its integer triangular basis for the chosen order. In particular $A_n$ has an integer expansion in that basis. Its elements are also rationally independent: clear denominators in a finite rational relation and use their integer independence. Step 4 already expresses $A_n$ rationally in the positive-only part of exactly this triangular family (all negative and Cartan indices zero). Comparing the two finite expansions by that rational independence forces the Step 4 coefficients to be integers and every other triangular coefficient to be zero. Subtracting the integer coefficient $\varepsilon^n$ preserves integrality. Step 5 gives the strict exponent bound; Step 4 gives the required root support and weight. For $n=1$ these conditions leave no correction monomial, and the empty sum is permitted.
